question: An oropharyngeal airway (OPA) sized by measuring from the centre of the mouth to the angle of the mandible is correctly sized and will effectively maintain airway patency.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true. The standard sizing method for an OPA is to measure from the corner of the mouth (or centre of the mouth) to the angle of the mandible. An OPA too short will not bypass the tongue; one too long may push the epiglottis down and worsen obstruction.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Measuring from the centre of the mouth (or the corner of the mouth) to the angle of the jaw gives the approximate length needed for the OPA tip to sit just behind the tongue base without impinging on the epiglottis or larynx.
